questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Rome because I have a personal interest in Roman history and I also wanted to explore Italy. It was also important to me to go to a country within the EU in order to study courses with an EU-perspective

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, the university was very helpful. However, I had to seek out a lot of information on my own, since the amount of official information that is sent out without you prompting it is very minimal, making it very confusing.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a lot of technical troubles with the platforms used, that the university was very quick in clearing up for me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through a secure rental website, but it was very difficult to find something within a student-friendly budget in attractive areas of the city, and there are a lot of scammers on housing pages on facebook etc.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very important to live near a metroline, as the traffic can be very heavy in the city and the busses are thus not very reliable. Also, depending on where you live, the transportation time can be very long.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to sign up through their own platform with a learning agreement a long time before the learning agreements could actually be made, so it had to be provisional.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to contact the mobility office of the host institution on email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was registered for all the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just check to make sure you have all the documents required when signing up, or write the host institution if you have any doubts

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The courses were quite easy to pass, however, it was very difficult to find out what level the professors expected from you. But overall the work load was quite light, since the professors usually didn't expect you to do the readings for the classes, and reading slides was sufficient for passing all the courses. 

There was also a general lack of information about exams, assessment criteria etc. for most of the courses, and in practice, most of the courses were a chaotic in the day-to-day

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was no group work in most classes, and the teaching was mainly the professors lecturing, but with some student participation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Regulatory Innovation
Media Law
European Private Law
International Arbitration
Diplomacy and Negotiation

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International arbitration was very practically oriented with professors who worked in the field, so if you have an interest in procedural and arbitration law, it gave a very practical insight.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Eating out and drinks were more expensive than I had expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out and drinks were generally more expensive. Museums etc. usually had a large discount for students under 26, so were very cheap, usually 2 euros.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not use any non-academic opportunities, so I cannot assess whether they were satisfactory.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many different kind of sports clubs, language courses etc. were available, but due to overlapping classes and living quite far away from campus, I didn't make use of the opportunities

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not attend any of the activities, so I cannot make a personal recommendation.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Many museums are very cheap for students, and from Rome you can take many day/weekendtrips to the surrounding area.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to use the study cafes and bars at the biggest campus, since most english courses will not have many local students attending.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences particularly challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The easygoingness and general helpfulness and cheerfulness was very nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Sign up for housing through the university near campus
Make an effort socially, since the format of the classes do not help in connecting to your co-students
Take it one step at a time with the courses, since they are quite unstructured and you cannot do anything to change that - and everything always works out anyway.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in a new city and getting to know people from all over.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Mainly also keeping in touch with Denmark, as I had to apply for new classes etc. and remembering to keep an eye out on KU-mail was pretty difficult as I felt very far removed from the daily life in Denmark.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
